fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Walkway; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and prevent branches from blocking emergency vehicles.
• Keep a minimum of one vehicle-width of clearance on the access drive at all times.
• Clear vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure to allow responders to move between the two buildings without obstruction.
• Mark or label the rear access point so responders arriving from the front can quickly locate it.
• Keep the rear access point unlocked or fitted with a knox-box style lockbox to allow responders through without delay.
• Trim dense vegetation near the rear of the property to allow responders to move and stage equipment safely.
• Keep the walkway clear of stored items, equipment, or overgrown plantings that would slow responder movement.
• Post the property address visibly at the road and again at the main entrance to the residence.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Grass Cover; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Along Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees close to the structure so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Cut grass around the structure short and keep it mowed regularly, especially during dry periods.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Separate any shrubs growing beneath or between trees near the structure so fire cannot move easily from shrubs up into the trees.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including emergency equipment, can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep vegetation along the driveway edges cut back to maintain clear sightlines and room for vehicles to move and turn around.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from around the base of the structure and near scattered shrubs.
• Keep the open green space areas mowed and free of accumulated dry grass or debris.
